Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the MediCore Health System Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold as it may be audible to the group. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MediCore Health System's financial results for the second quarter of 2024. Joining me on the call are John Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Sarah Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Medical Officer; Michael Reyes, Chief Operating Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Strategy Officer; and David Kim, Chief Information Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to John Hale.

John Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter of 2024. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on seven key aspects: trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, trends in payer mix shifts and their impact on revenue, impact of recent acquisitions on financial performance, trends in staffing levels and contract labor usage, impact of seasonality or external factors such as flu season, overview of key financial performance highlights, and net patient revenue year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter.

Let me start with trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, a structural shift that's reshaping our business through payer policies, technology, and patient preferences, and we're positioning MediCore to thrive in it. System-wide, inpatient admissions totaled 142,000 for the quarter, down 4.2% from last year, consistent with industry patterns seen at companies like HCA Healthcare and Tenet. This drop ties to lower-acuity cases moving outpatient, plus a 2.1% shorter average length of stay at 4.6 days—our lowest in five years. That said, it's not uniform erosion; our case mix index rose 3.8% to 1.92, showing we're handling more complex inpatient cases like cardiac ablations and orthopedic revisions. Inpatient revenue per admission stayed at $14,200, bolstered by Medicare's 2.6% IPPS update for fiscal 2024.

On the flip side, outpatient volumes jumped 8.7% year-over-year to 1.76 million encounters, led by a 12.4% rise in ambulatory surgery center cases—now 28% of total surgical volume—along with 9.2% growth in imaging and infusion. Observation stays increased 6.1% but were flat sequentially amid CMS two-midnight rule oversight. Outpatient revenue per visit rose 5.3% to $1,450, thanks to demand for high-margin endoscopy and pain management. Surgical trends highlight this: inpatient surgeries fell 7.1% to 48,000, while outpatient and ASC procedures soared 14.2% to 112,000, echoing CDC data where outpatient visits outpace inpatient 3-to-1 since 2020. Post-COVID demand has settled, but site-neutral payments from CMS's 2024 OPPS rule make ASCs more attractive.

By region, Southeast markets like Florida and Georgia—18 hospitals and 25 ASCs—saw outpatient growth hit 11.3%, driven by 42% Medicare Advantage mix and Humana bundles for orthopedics. Florida's seniors and tourism boosted elective ortho and ophthalmology by 16%. In the Midwest, Ohio and Michigan's 12 facilities grew outpatient 6.2%, tempered by physician-owned ASC competition and USPI, with inpatient down 6.8% from Medicaid redeterminations cutting payer favorability by 1.5 points.

We're advancing with our Epic MyChart rollout, live in 85% of sites, improving outpatient scheduling 22% and enabling same-day access—key to 15% sequential clinic growth. We've added 12 da Vinci robots quarter-over-quarter, 68% in outpatient for hysterectomies and hernias with faster recovery. Nuance Dragon Ambient eXperience grew virtual consults 28%, especially rural. This fits our 'Outpatient First' strategy: seven new ASCs by year-end for $250 million EBITDA by 2026 in GI and musculoskeletal, plus joint ventures with ortho groups for 10 ED-ASC hybrids like Tenet's approach. We're pushing site-neutral carve-outs via the Federation of American Hospitals and 22 value-based contracts for 15% of lives on total care costs.

Ahead, inpatient should stabilize with mid-single-digit CMI growth into 2025, outpatient to low-double-digits on flu tailwinds and $450 million capex, targeting 5-7% revenue growth and outpatient margins to 22% from 19.5%.

Next, trends in payer mix shifts and their revenue effects, a core driver we're managing proactively. For Q2, Medicare was 47% of net patient revenue, up from 45% last year and 44% in Q1. Commercial payers like UnitedHealthcare, Anthem, and Cigna were 34%, down 150 basis points from 35.5%. Medicaid steady at 12%, self-pay and others 7%—similar to HCA and Tenet, reflecting our high-acuity focus.

Industry-wide, Medicare Advantage hit 52% of eligibles per CMS, up from 48%, with Humana and United expanding benefits for Boomers, pushing delegated risk our way. Commercial dipped from 2% fewer employer PPOs per Kaiser, shifting to HDHPs post-No Surprises Act. Our net revenue per admission was $14,200, up 3.2% YoY, but payer variances show: commercial 25% above Medicare on DRG basis ($18,500 vs. $14,800 ortho). The Medicare shift cut NRPA growth by 1.5%; pro forma, $45 million quarterly headwind across 28 hospitals. It slowed adjusted admissions to 2.1% YoY, as Medicare has shorter stays, lower elective acuity.

Regions differ: Northeast (Boston, Philly) holds 42% commercial from biotech and academics, with 5% outpatient revenue per visit growth. Southeast Medicaid at 18% vs. 10% national, Georgia/North Carolina redeterminations added lives at 15% below Medicare. West Coast California Medi-Cal at 60% MA, but DPH supplements lifted NRPA 2%.

We're countering with value-based: 22% Medicare in ACO REACH/Next Gen, up from 15%, yielding $28 million shared savings from 14.2% heart failure readmissions via CarePathway and Epic-SNF links. Humana risk contracts for 180,000 Florida/Texas lives at 80/20 splits, 8% ortho/cardio margins vs. 4% FFS. Commercial: 4-6% uplifts on 65% book from BCBS, piloting employer direct contracting at Medicare+150% for 5% now, 12% year-end. Labor optimized, California Prop 1 ratios via float pools at 28% revenue.

Forward, Medicare to 48-49% in 2025 on 2.9% IPPS, commercial to 33% on HDHPs. Guidance has $120-150 million offset, offset by 3% volumes, 2.5% pricing for 4-5% growth, EBITDA margins +50 bps to 12.5%.

Moving to the impact of recent acquisitions on our financials, a major growth engine. Over 12 months, three deals at $1.2 billion: $850 million Southeast Regional Health Network Q4 2023—seven hospitals, 1,800 beds in Florida/Georgia/Carolinas with 2-3% Census growth. $250 million 12 Midwest ASCs Q1 2024 for ortho/GI in Ohio/Indiana. $100 million 15 Texas cardio practices for vertical integration.

They added $285 million to Q2 revenue—18% of $1.58 billion total, +12% YoY reported, 7% same-facility. Pro forma, Southeast $220 million, 55% commercial, 30% MA (stable vs. 15-20% denials), 15% Medicaid. EBITDA $65 million at 23% margin—400 bps above average—on 1.85 CMI vs. 1.72 legacy, 4.2-day ALOS, 72% occupancy. $0.28 EPS accretion net $12 million integration for Epic/supply chain. YTD $35 million synergies vs. $50 million FY24 target: 15% procurement cuts with Medtronic/Cardinal like HCA's Mission; 25% agency via RN cross-training (AMN rates 20% above pre-COVID); 8% collections via AI denial tool.

Southeast: #2 behind HCA, 12% share Jacksonville/Charlotte, +14% QoQ admissions on post-respiratory electives, Optum cardiology JV. Midwest ASCs +22% ortho, 45% margins vs. 35% VMG. Diversifies to 22% EBITDA cardio from 16%, TAM +25% to $45 billion. Tele-ICU with Philips cuts readmissions 12%, CCJR savings. H2 10-12% growth, $0.75 full-year EPS.

These transform us amid MA resets/labor, like Tenet's Vanderbilt, CHS divestitures; 5-7% same-facility, 25%+ margins long-term.

On trends in staffing levels and contract labor, key to 320 bps EBITDA margin expansion to 18.2%. Total FTEs 52,400, +2.8% YoY, mainly 1,200 RNs for 4.1% adjusted admissions in ortho/cardio. 7.2 RN FTEs per occupied bed vs. 6.9, per CMS metrics.

RN turnover 16.8% from 28.4% peak via $45 million "Stay MediCore"—bonuses, tuition, 22% voluntary exit drop. Ratios 1:4.5 med-surg vs. 1:5.8, HCAHPS +4 to 72%.

Contract nursing hours 9.2% vs. 14.7%, dollars -31% QoQ to $128 million (4.1% labor vs. 6.8%), like HCA/UHS; AMN ICU rates $110 vs. $185 peak, -35-40%. Locums 3% hours, travel 72%; vendor cuts 40% at 15-20% below spot.

Sunbelt (Texas/Florida, 62% beds) <8% contract, organic 450 Dallas RNs. Coastal CA/Northeast 12-14% on AB 394/$120 wages; Chamberlain partnership 150 LPN-RNs.

Qventus AI at 85% sites: 15% OT cut, 12% agency drop via Epic acuity. Workday Talent Hub: 2,800 floats, -18% external. Incredible Health bots for 25% faster hires.

Labor 52.4% revenue, -210 bps; $150 million plan for $220 million FY26 savings, contract <7%, turnover <15%. Raised FY24 EBITDA $1.85-1.92 billion.

Regarding impact of seasonality and external factors like flu season, a predictable driver in our 45 hospitals/120 ASCs across 12 states. Q1 fiscal (calendar Q4-Jan) peaks respiratory: typical severe +18-25% admissions QoQ, +8-12% total, ADC +10%, days +9%, +7% adjusted. ICU +15%, $14,500 DRG-CMI revenue, 52% commercial.

This Q2 moderate: 2.1% flu positivity CDC, ER +16% QoQ (45,000 visits), admissions +9% to 128,000, $285 million revenue (+4.2% of $6.8 billion), hospital EBITDA +120 bps to 18.7%. Antivirals +22% to $42 million, Vizient 11% discounts.

Northeast +28% peds/13% ADC RSV; Sunbelt +6%, elective offset. CMI 1.92, Northeast MS-DRG 207 pop. Vortex traumas +5%; vax 68% cut hospitalizations 22%. IPPS 2.9% tailwind, Medicaid unwind -1.5% mix, +$18 million bad debt.

Epic-HHS AI forecasts 88% bed demand accuracy; Workforce Center caps labor 8%; telehealth 14,000 visits saves 2,500 beds. $450 million capex +300 ICUs. FY25 Q1 +7-9% admissions, +100-150 bps margins; RSV Beyfortus pilot.

Net positive $1.1 billion annual flu revenue, managed for growth.

For an overview of key financial performance highlights, we posted $2.48 billion net revenues, +9.2% YoY, 7.8% same-hospital—eighth straight quarter. Inpatient admissions +4.1% to 142,000, days +5.3% to 1.1 million. Outpatient 58% revenue (from 54%), +14.2%, ASCs +22% on site-neutral.

EBITDA $512 million, +13.5%, margins +110 bps to 20.6%; $28 million productivity. Net income $185 million, $1.42 EPS (+$0.08 guide); adjusted $1.51 post $15 million divestiture gain.

Op ex $1.97 billion +7.9%; labor 52% +8.2% on 15% agency premiums (AHA), but contract 4.2% vs. 6.1% via Talent Pipeline 2,800 permanents. Supply +6.5%, 3% GPO ortho/pharma.

Southeast 60% beds +6.2% admissions, 32% MA +300 bps, Florida post-Ian. Midwest +3.4%, $150 million ASC pivot. Epic 8 go-lives +2.5% cycle, denial 4.8% vs. 7.2%; Google CMI +1.8% to 1.92. Capex $220 million (8.9%), $400 million FY24 +500 beds.

Debt/EBITDA 3.1x from 3.4x, $450 million FCF, $100 million buyback, dividend +5% to $0.22. Raised FY23 rev $9.95-10.05 billion, EBITDA $1.98-2.02; Q4 $2.52-2.56 billion, 20.5% margins. Navigates IPPS/MA via outpatient/value-based.

Finally, net patient revenue at $2.48 billion, +8.7% YoY, +4.2% QoQ from $2.38 billion—beats HCA's 7%, vs. payer shifts/Medicaid.

YoY $198 million growth: volume 45% ($89 million)—admissions +5.2% to 78,400, elective +12% ortho/PCI to 95% pre-COVID, outpatient +9.8%, obs +14% Teladoc; ADC 2,450, ALOS 4.6 days -2% Epic no-shows -18%.

Acuity/mix 35% ($69 million): CMI +3.1% 1.82 surgical DRGs 470/252; Medicare 42%, Medicaid 22% (-redeterminations TX/FL), commercial 28%, other 8%; +2.5% BCBS. Pricing +4.1% per day, allowances 28.4%, bad debt 2.1% vs. 2.4% Waystar DSO 48.

QoQ +2.8% admissions, +6.1% outpatient, +1.2% CMI post-summer. Southeast 52% rev +11.2% Jacksonville ERs/Humana; Midwest 28% +6.4% Ohio unwind offset ortho; West 20% +7.9% CA AB72, +8% implants.

Validates High-Acuity Outpatient-First: $150 million ASCs (15 ops, 20% margins vs. 12%), Optum MSK +5% ASPs. Q4 +7-9% YoY, CMI 1.85, stable payers; risks IPPS cuts/labor, 98% nurse retention.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Sarah Thompson to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, John. Good morning, everyone. As John mentioned, we had a strong quarter. Net revenue for the second quarter of 2024 was $1.58 billion, an increase of 12% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $1.30 billion, representing 82% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in outpatient expansion.

Net income for the quarter was $185 million, or $1.42 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Chen for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Emily Chen:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our CarePathway program has shown promising results, with a 20% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform and remote patient monitoring programs.

Following that, Michael Reyes will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Michael Reyes:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including Epic MyChart implementation and da Vinci robotic surgery expansions, which have resulted in significant cost savings and improved patient flow.

Next, Lisa Patel will discuss our strategic initiatives.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. Our strategic priorities remain focused on expanding our network, developing new partnerships, and investing in innovative technologies. We are actively exploring opportunities to grow our footprint in key markets and enhance our service offerings.

After that, David Kim will discuss our IT infrastructure and cybersecurity.

David Kim:
Thank you, Lisa. We are committed to maintaining a robust and secure IT infrastructure to support our operations and protect patient data. We have implemented several new security measures to enhance our cybersecurity posture and ensure compliance with regulatory requirements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to John Hale.

John Hale:
Thank you, everyone. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Mark Johnson with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Mark Johnson:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of the recent cybersecurity threats on your operations and patient data?

David Kim:
Good morning, Mark. Recent cybersecurity threats have been top of mind across the industry, but at MediCore, we've seen no material impact on our operations or patient data. Our robust framework includes advanced AI-driven threat detection integrated with our Epic ecosystem, regular penetration testing, and zero-trust architecture rolled out across 100% of facilities this year. We've partnered with leading firms for continuous monitoring, and our incident response time averages under 30 minutes. Compliance with HIPAA and HITRUST remains flawless, and we're investing an additional $50 million in FY24 for quantum-resistant encryption and employee training to stay ahead of evolving risks.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
What are your plans for expanding your telehealth capabilities and remote patient monitoring programs?

Dr. Emily Chen:
Thanks, Sarah. Telehealth and remote monitoring are central to our patient-centered model. We've grown virtual consults 28% this quarter via Nuance integration, particularly for outpatient and rural access. Plans include scaling our platform to cover 50% of primary care visits by year-end, adding RPM for 100,000 chronic patients in heart failure and COPD via Philips wearables—already cutting readmissions 12%. Partnerships with Teladoc and Optum will bundle these into value-based episodes, targeting $100 million savings by 2026 while boosting satisfaction scores.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Wong with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Wong:
Can you provide more details on your strategic partnerships and their potential impact on your business?

Lisa Patel:
Absolutely, David. Our partnerships are accelerating growth. Recent JVs with ortho groups and Humana for bundles cover 15% of lives, driving ortho volumes +16% in Florida. Optum cardiology in Southeast yields 8% margins on episodes. We're negotiating 22 value-based contracts and direct employer deals at Medicare+150%, scaling to 12% commercial revenue. These de-risk mix shifts, expand TAM 25%, and support 10-12% H2 growth from acquired assets.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. On staffing, how sustainable is the contract labor reduction, and any updates on turnover?

Sarah Thompson:
Great question, Lisa. Our contract usage at 9.2% is sustainable, down sharply as markets normalize—AMN rates -35%. Qventus AI and Talent Hub cut fills 18%, with organic Sunbelt hires strong. Turnover at 16.8% via incentives; targeting <15% year-end. This underpins labor at 52.4% revenue, freeing capex for ASCs.

John Hale:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the MediCore Health System Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
